Getting around. The rules.

Ojai is a small town in a valley in Ventura County with one car-free path, one gravel mountain and one long highway climb. The Ojai Valley Trail runs 9.3 paved miles from Bryant Street to Foster Park and on to Ventura, about 15 miles in all. Sulphur Mountain Road is 9 miles of gated dirt, and Highway 33 climbs 10.8 miles into Los Padres National Forest. Center Ride Out, the Los Angeles LGBT Center’s three-day ride, camps in Ojai on April 23–25, 2027. There’s no airport and no train, so plan on a car to get here. Santa Barbara is the closest airport, about 34 miles west in a straight line.

Best months
November to May for the dirt. Bikepacking.com gives that window for the Ojai Rim Loop and calls February and March best, when it’s cooler and the creeks run. Pathless Pedaled says to ride Sulphur Mountain in the cooler months. Inland Ojai is hot in summer, so start early then.
Nearest airport
Santa Barbara Airport (SBA), 34 mi
Major airport
Los Angeles International (LAX), 59 mi

Clubs and collectives in Ojai

  1. Easy Rider (Channel Islands Bicycle Club and BikeVentura)

    Beginner friendlyNo-drop

    The closest thing to a group ride into the Ojai Valley. Free rides from the Museum of Ventura County lot, in two groups: Easy Rider and a longer Easy Rider Plus. The group calls them beginner-friendly and no-drop. Its Nov 15, 2026 ride sent the Plus group up the path to Meiners Oaks, about 29 miles round trip. Sign the online waiver first, and be able to ride 20 miles at 12 mph. Day and time: the Easy Rider ride (Every other Sunday, 9:00 am).

    In the directory: Easy Rider Community Ride (Every other Sunday, 9:00 am) →

  2. Channel Islands Bicycle Club

    A road club in Ventura that describes itself as social riding. Weekly rides leave from Ventura, and special rides come up to Ojai. It posted a Sulphur Mountain gravel and road loop into Ojai for April 2, 2026: 47 miles from the Museum lot or 32 from the Sulphur Mountain trailhead, with lunch in Meiners Oaks. Ride as a member, or sign the ride waiver on the club’s calendar page.

    In the directory: Saturday Up the Pacific Coast (Channel Islands Bicycle Club) (Saturdays, 8:00 am); Saturday Montecito and Summerland (Channel Islands Bicycle Club) (Saturdays, 8:30 am); Sunday Canyon to Canyon (Channel Islands Bicycle Club) (Sundays, 8:00 am) →

  3. Great Outdoors — Santa Barbara Ventura County chapter

    LGBTQ+

    An all-volunteer LGBTQIA+ and allies outdoors club, not a cycling club. It hikes and camps. It has led a bike ride from Ventura up the trail to Ojai and back: 30 miles at a pace it called leisurely, with lunch in downtown Ojai (Nov 23, 2025). No bike ride was on its calendar on Nov 15, 2026, so check the outings page. Register for an outing on the site. Membership is $25 a year (Nov 2026).

How Ojai rides: the zones, getting here

About Ojai

Ojai sits in a valley in Ventura County at 745 feet: 7,637 people at the 2020 census, in 4.4 square miles. This guide covers the town and the valley around it. That’s Meiners Oaks and the west end toward Lake Casitas. Mira Monte, Oak View and Casitas Springs down the bike path. Upper Ojai over the hill to the east. Ventura, about 12 miles south, is a different town. It’s here only for the shops that are open when Ojai’s is shut and the clubs that ride up the path.

It’s written for two readers. The first is the Center Ride Out rider. The ride reaches Ojai on Friday, April 23, 2027. Riders can stay in camp or ride an out-and-back on Saturday. They roll for Los Angeles by 7:00 am on Sunday. The Center has not published where the camp is. Saturday is the day for coffee, a shop and a short ride. The second reader is whoever drives up to meet them and needs a room. Or anyone who comes with a bike on another weekend.

Ojai is one of everything. One bike shop, The Mob Shop, downtown and closed Tuesday and Wednesday. One coffee place open at 6 every day, Ojai Coffee Roasters. We found no recurring group ride that starts in the valley. The rides that reach it come up the path from Ventura. Dinner ends early: most kitchens close by 8 or 9.

Riding in Ojai

Start with the Ojai Valley Trail. It’s a paved rail-trail, car-free, 9.3 miles from Bryant Street in Ojai down to Foster Park. There the Ventura River Trail carries on to the coast, about 15 miles in all. It drops gently the whole way, so the climb is on the way home: about 500 feet from Foster Park, 800 to 1,000 from Ventura. Weekends are crowded and the pavement has root bumps.

The short road climb is the Upper Ojai Summit: 6.5 miles and 781 feet east out of town on a two-lane road with narrow shoulders. The long one is Highway 33 north: 10.8 miles and 2,625 feet at 4.6 percent. It goes through the three Wheeler Gorge tunnels, and there’s no water you can count on. Caltrans is rebuilding those tunnels and expects to finish in winter 2026/2027, so check State Route 33 before you go. The long road day is the Lake Casitas loop, 48 miles out Highway 150 to the coast and home up the path.

The gravel is Sulphur Mountain Road: about 9 miles and 2,100 feet of gated ranch road. Cattle on it, no cars, no water and little shade. Ride it as a 30-mile loop from town. The Ojai Rim Loop is the two-day version, 67 miles and 10,277 feet. Both are for the cooler months.

The 6 routes, with maps →

Getting to Ojai

Drive. Ojai has no airport and no train. Santa Barbara Airport (SBA) is the closest with airlines, about 34 miles west in a straight line. Hollywood Burbank is about 54 and Los Angeles International about 59 southeast. The drive is longer than each number. From the south or the coast, take the 101 to Ventura and Highway 33 north, 14 miles to town. Route 150 over Casitas Pass also comes in from the 101. The Ojai Valley Inn’s directions page says to skip it in rain, at night or if you don’t know the road (Nov 2026). Without a car: Gold Coast Transit Route 16 links the Ventura Transit Center with downtown Ojai. Every bus has a front rack for three built bikes, free. The nearest train is the Pacific Surfliner in Ventura, where a full-size bike rides free with a reserved bike space. Ventura is the bottom of the bike path, about 15 miles below Ojai.

Questions about riding in Ojai

Which Ojai hotels have complimentary bikes for guests?

Four say so on their own pages. Ojai Rancho Inn lists “Complimentary bicycles for use,” Hummingbird Inn says “grab a complimentary bicycle and tour Ojai,” Casa Ojai Inn lists “Bicycles, Locks, and Helmets included with amenity fee,” and Ojai Valley Inn says “Pick up a complimentary Linus bicycle.” None of them states a policy on bringing your own bike into the room, so ask when you book.

What coffee shop in Ojai opens at 6 a.m.?

Ojai Coffee Roasters, downtown at 337 E. Ojai Ave., opens at 6 a.m. every day, Saturday and Sunday included; its kitchen runs 9 to 2. Coffee Connection in Meiners Oaks opens at 6 on Saturday and closes at 1, but its Sunday hours aren’t settled, so call first.

Where can I rent a road bike in Ojai?

The Mob Shop, 110 W Ojai Ave. It rents an ENVE Melee road bike in 54, 56 and 58, plus gravel and mountain bikes, by advance booking only, with no walk-ins, and it’s closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Its rental pages say these bikes “may not be rented for mass start events or races,” so ask the shop before you plan one for an organized ride.

How long is the Ojai Valley Trail, and is it paved?

It’s 9.3 miles and paved, a car-free rail-trail from Bryant Street in Ojai to Foster Park. There it meets the Ventura River Trail, which makes about 15 miles one way from Ojai to Ventura. Some stretches are bumpy and cracked from tree roots, and it gets crowded on weekends.

Should I bring my bike to Ojai?

Yes, and plan on a car, because Ojai has no airport and no train. Delta, American and Southwest check a packed bike at the standard bag fee (Nov 2026), and Ojai’s one rental shop is book-ahead only and closed Tuesday and Wednesday. No shop in the Ojai Valley or Ventura says it receives a shipped bike.

Where do Center Ride Out riders sleep in Ojai?

They camp. The ride reaches Ojai on Friday, April 23, 2027 and rolls for Los Angeles by 7:00 am on Sunday, and the Center has not published where the camp is. The hotels in this guide are for whoever drives up to meet a rider.
